Generic dispatcher for loo / waic on ame / lame fits

Source: R/loo_methods.R
loo.Rd

Lightweight S3 generics so calls of the form loo(fit) dispatch through R's S3 system even when the loo package is not loaded. When loo is loaded, its generic resolves first; this fallback only fires for bare-namespace use.

Usage

loo(x, ...)

waic(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a fitted ame or lame object with $log_lik.

...

passed to the relevant method.

Value

A loo / waic object.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 12
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * n), n, n); diag(Y) <- NA
# a model without actor effects; chains = 1 keeps the example short
fit <- ame(Y, R = 0, rvar = FALSE, cvar = FALSE, dcor = FALSE,
           nscan = 200, burn = 20, odens = 1,
           save_log_lik = TRUE, verbose = FALSE, chains = 1)
if (requireNamespace("loo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(loo(fit))
  print(waic(fit))
}
#> 
#> Computed from 200 by 132 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>          Estimate   SE
#> elpd_loo   -172.9  7.9
#> p_loo         2.1  0.3
#> looic       345.8 15.8
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.1.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume independent draws (r_eff=1).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.57).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> 
#> Computed from 200 by 132 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>           Estimate   SE
#> elpd_waic   -172.8  7.9
#> p_waic         2.0  0.3
#> waic         345.7 15.8
# }
